job.title: Chief Financial Officer
job.description:
• Shape and guide sound finanical perfomance and systems while building a modern corporate finance function.
  • Be a key strategic adviser to the SLT and Chief Executive.
  • Embed and enhance finance technology uplift, leading the business through this change.


The Office of the Auditor-General has a unique constitutional role, independently assuring Parliament and the public that public organisations operate and account for their performance as Parliament intended.


About this role | Mō tēnei tūranga
Reporting to the Assistant Auditor-General, Enablement, the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) leads the Audit Office's financial strategy, performance, and long-term sustainability.

Join The Audit Office at a pivotal stage to develop a modern, high-performing finance function. You will transform financial strategy, reporting, systems, and business insight to provide a step-change in organisational decision-making.

As a trusted adviser to the Assistant Auditor-General, Enablement, the Auditor-General, Deputy Auditor-General, and Senior Leadership Team, you will provide influential financial leadership and guide investment and funding decisions to deliver strategic objectives. Your confidence, credibility, and sound judgement will enable candid advice and constructive challenge, shaping decisions that support the Audit Office's long-term effectiveness and impact.


Key responsibilities include:

  • Providing strategic advice on financial performance, funding, investment, risk, and long-term sustainability.
  • Leading and developing a high-performing Finance team with a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and professional excellence.
  • Developing a modern, high-performing finance function, including capability, systems, processes, and operating models.
  • Improving financial reporting, forecasting, costing, and decision support for better organisational outcomes.
  • Driving organisational efficiency, continuous improvement, and value-for-money initiatives.
  • Leading budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, business partnering, and strategic financial planning.
  • Leading ongoing FMIS development and optimisation to realise investment benefits.
  • Building strong relationships with Treasury and other key stakeholders.

As a member of the Enablement Leadership Team and wider Office leadership team, you will contribute to the Office's long-term success and its unique role strengthening trust, transparency, and accountability across New Zealand's public sector.


About you | Mōhou ake
You are an experienced finance executive with strong strategic capability, sound judgement, and proven executive-level influence. You combine commercial acumen with a passion for continuous improvement and are comfortable leading change in complex environments.

You will bring:

  • Significant senior financial leadership experience at Tier 3 level or above.
  • Proven people leadership experience, including developing high-performing teams.
  • Expertise in financial analysis, forecasting, budgeting, and performance management.
  • Experience providing trusted advice to executive leadership teams.
  • A proven record of transforming finance functions, improving reporting and decision support, and delivering efficiencies through finance systems, operating model, and process improvements.
  • Experience delivering benefits from FMIS or comparable finance system implementations.
  • Knowledge of public sector financial management and government accounting requirements.
  • Strong stakeholder management and relationship-building skills.
  • CA qualification and a relevant tertiary qualification.


About our group and team | Mātau rōpū ake

  • The Enablement Group consists of our Finance team, Digital team, People and Capability team, Property and Infrastructure team, and our Security and risk function. This role forms part of an important cohort of Enablement leaders that work together to drive meaningful change and strategic implementation across the Office.
  • Within the Enablement Group, the Finance team provides financial stewardship, planning, reporting, advisory, treasury, payroll, and accountability services underpinning the Office's performance and effectiveness.


Are you ready to make a difference? | Kua rite koe mō tēnei mahi?
If providing strategic financial leadership in an organisation supporting the integrity of New Zealand's public sector motivates you, we welcome your interest.

For a confidential discussion, contact Charlotte Cottrell at INSIDE Recruitment on 04 913 6944 or charlotte@inside.co.nz.

Applications close: 4pm Friday, 20th November.

The Office of the Auditor-General is committed to a diverse, inclusive, and respectful workplace. Please let us know if you require any adjustments to participate fully in the recruitment process.

job.title: General Manager Technology
job.description:
• Shape the technology future of a newly established national Crown agency.
  • Lead a major multi-year programme of technology renewal and transformation.
  • Location for this role is flexible.


Help shape the future of school property in Aotearoa
The New Zealand School Property Agency (NZSPA) was established in October 2026 as a standalone Crown entity responsible for managing New Zealand’s school property portfolio on behalf of the Government. We build, maintain and oversee the infrastructure that helps children and young people learn and thrive. Our priorities are to deliver better value for taxpayers, improve service to schools, and provide greater transparency around property planning and school entitlements.


About this role | Mō tēnei tūranga
This is a rare opportunity to shape the technology future of a newly established national crown agency. Reporting directly to the Chief Executive and serving on the Executive Leadership Team, the General Manager Information Technology will set NZSPA’s enterprise technology and digital direction, build the capability required of a standalone organisation and lead a significant programme of renewal and transformation.

You will guide a multi-year technology investment programme, with the potential to increase as requirements are confirmed. The challenge includes transitioning from Ministry of Education systems and services, replacing end-of-life platforms, reducing manual processes and enabling modern asset management across a school property portfolio valued at more than $30 billion.

You will balance ambitious transformation with secure, resilient day-to-day technology services, while advising the Chief Executive and Board on investment priorities, delivery, cyber risk and measurable outcomes.


About you | Mōhou ake
We are looking for an accomplished and experienced technology executive who combines strategic vision with pragmatic delivery, commercial judgement and the ability to lead change across a complex organisation. You will bring:

  • Substantial senior technology leadership experience, ideally at CIO, CDO or General Manager level.
  • A strong track record of leading multi-year technology renewal, legacy replacement and business transformation programmes that deliver tangible organisational/system outcomes and positive change
  • Experience with enterprise platforms, information and data governance, and preferably asset management, property or infrastructure systems.
  • Sound judgement in technology investment, supplier management, cyber security, risk and operational resilience.
  • The ability to work with Boards, chief executives and senior colleagues, build capable teams and deliver change while maintaining essential services.
  • A commitment to public service integrity, collaboration, inclusion and accountability.


About our group and team | Mātau rōpū ake
The technology function will play a central role in NZSPA’s establishment and ongoing effectiveness. Working with executive colleagues across asset management, planning, investment, procurement and supplier management, you will help create integrated systems, trusted information and practical digital services that support better decisions and outcomes for schools. The structure and reporting arrangements below the executive level are subject to further organisational design and consultation.


Are you ready to make a difference? | Kua rite koe mō tēnei mahi?
If you are motivated by the opportunity to build something enduring and deliver technology change with a clear public purpose, we would welcome your interest.

Please submit your CV and a cover letter outlining your motivation and relevant experience.

For a confidential discussion, contact Nick Ritchie at INSIDE Recruitment on 022 096 3399.

Applications close: 4pm Wednesday, 18th November.

NZSPA is committed to a diverse, inclusive and respectful workplace. Please let us know if you require assistance or adjustments to participate fully in the recruitment process. Appointment is subject to applicable security clearance and Police vetting requirements.

job.title: Chief Financial Officer
job.description:
• Shape investment decisions while building a modern corporate finance function.
  • Be a key strategic adviser to the Chief Executive and Board.
  • Location for this role is flexible.


Help shape the future of school property in Aotearoa
The New Zealand School Property Agency (NZSPA) was established in October 2026 as a standalone Crown entity responsible for managing New Zealand’s school property portfolio on behalf of the Government. We build, maintain and oversee the infrastructure that helps children and young people learn and thrive. Our priorities are to deliver better value for taxpayers, improve service to schools, and provide greater transparency around property planning and school entitlements.


About this role | Mō tēnei tūranga
This is an exceptional opportunity to shape the financial and corporate foundations of a newly established national Crown entity. Reporting directly to the Chief Executive and serving on the Executive Leadership Team, the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) will lead NZSPA’s finance, risk, and assurance portfolios, providing strategic advice and strong stewardship of public resources.

As the key strategic financial adviser to the Chief Executive and Board, you will help guide investment decisions and long-term sustainability across a school property portfolio valued at more than $30 billion. You will establish the agency’s financial management systems, planning, budgeting, reporting, controls and statutory accounts, while ensuring that commercial and assurance advice supports practical delivery and value for money.

You will lead a broad portfolio through organisational establishment and change, building integrated financial and corporate capabilities, strengthening public accountability and helping NZSPA deliver better outcomes for schools and communities.


About you | Mōhou ake
We are seeking an accomplished finance executive who combines strategic financial stewardship, sound commercial judgement and the ability to build high-performing teams through change. You will bring:

  • A Chartered Accountant or equivalent professional qualification, with extensive senior finance leadership experience, ideally at CFO or equivalent level.
  • A strong record of leading organisational transformation, establishing financial systems and controls, and improving performance and accountability.
  • Deep knowledge of public sector financial management, appropriations, Budget processes and statutory reporting, ideally gained in a Crown entity or comparable environment.
  • Experience providing trusted advice to chief executives and Boards, and overseeing or working closely with commercial, risk and assurance functions.
  • The ability to lead substantial professional teams, influence central agencies and auditors, and offer clear, independent advice on complex investment and financial decisions.
  • A commitment to public service integrity, collaboration, inclusion and accountability.
  • Deep understanding of the financial, commercial, and operational drivers underpinning education property portfolios and long-term asset sustainability.
  • Proven ability to balance strategic property investment decisions with organisational, community, and educational outcomes.


About our group and team | Mātau rōpū ake
The CFO portfolio brings together finance, risk, and assurance. You will work alongside executive colleagues to establish fit-for-purpose systems, governance and services that enable effective investment, operations and long-term stewardship of the school property portfolio. The proposed portfolio includes responsibility for a large team with final team structures and reporting arrangements subject to further organisational design and consultation.


Are you ready to make a difference? | Kua rite koe mō tēnei mahi?
If you are motivated by the opportunity to establish enduring financial and corporate capability in an organisation with a clear public purpose, we would welcome your interest.

For a confidential discussion, contact Charlotte Cottrell at INSIDE Recruitment on 04 913 6944.

Applications close: 4pm Wednesday, 18th November.

NZSPA is committed to a diverse, inclusive and respectful workplace. Please let us know if you require assistance or adjustments to participate fully in the recruitment process.

job.title: Senior Database Administrator
job.description:
• Make a meaningful impact supporting services across Aotearoa
  • Enjoy a strong benefits package, including wellbeing and health insurance support


We're looking for an experienced Database Administrator with strong PostgreSQL expertise to join an established team supporting critical database environments.

This is a hands-on role focused on managing, maintaining and optimising PostgreSQL databases, ensuring performance, security, availability and data integrity. You'll work across database administration, troubleshooting, recovery and migrations, with opportunities to contribute to cloud infrastructure and automation.


What you'll bring

  • Strong, proven experience as a Database Administrator, with a focus on PostgreSQL.
  • Experience managing and optimising PostgreSQL databases in production environments.
  • Knowledge of database performance tuning, security, backup and recovery.
  • Experience with AWS database services
  • Experience troubleshooting database issues and supporting migrations.
  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work collaboratively.

Experience with AWS CDK, infrastructure-as-code tools and database automation would be advantageous.

  • Permanent role with a salary of $120,000–$160,000, depending on experience.
  • An established, collaborative team and interesting technical challenges.
  • The opportunity to support critical systems and contribute to ongoing improvements.
  • Whilst Wellington is a preferred location, we’re open to applications throughout New Zealand.


Please click to apply now, or for a confidential discussion, please reach out to Alice Clark at alice@inside.co.nz.

Please note you must have valid New Zealand working rights.

job.title: Product Owner
job.description:
• Work in an established product practice with proven tools and frameworks.
  • Partner with Product leaders to influence strategy and product growth.
  • Turn customer insights into products that deliver measurable value.


INSIDE is pleased to partner with PartsTrader, a global market leader transforming the collision repair industry through innovative technology solutions. PartsTrader connects repairers, suppliers, insurers, and manufacturers through a powerful B2B marketplace platform, helping customers streamline operations, improve purchasing outcomes, and drive greater efficiency across the automotive ecosystem. With a strong presence in the US market and a reputation for innovation, PartsTrader is focused on delivering products that create measurable value for its customers.

Are you a commercially minded Product Owner who thrives on solving complex customer challenges and shaping products that deliver real business value?

We're looking for an experienced Product Owner to join a high-performing product team. Reporting to the Product Practice Lead, you'll work under the direction of the Head of Product to deliver strategically significant initiatives across the US market. This is a unique opportunity to influence product direction, partner with senior stakeholders, and help drive growth in a scaling B2B environment.

You'll act as the bridge between customers, business stakeholders, and delivery teams, ensuring product priorities are aligned to strategic goals and customer needs. This role is ideal for someone who enjoys turning market insights and customer feedback into tangible product outcomes.


What you'll be doing

  • Partner closely with Product leadership to shape and execute product strategy.
  • Own and prioritise the product backlog, balancing customer, commercial, and business needs.
  • Work with cross-functional teams to deliver high-value product enhancements and initiatives.
  • Engage with customers and stakeholders to understand challenges, opportunities, and emerging needs.
  • Use data, insights, and market trends to drive informed product decisions.
  • Translate business objectives into clear requirements and actionable delivery plans.
  • Contribute to product roadmaps that support growth across the US market.


What you'll bring

  • Proven Product Owner experience within a B2B product environment.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and relationship management skills.
  • Experience working alongside Product Managers and delivery teams in agile environments.
  • Ability to balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution.
  • Strong commercial acumen and customer-centric mindset.
  • Experience using customer insights, data, and feedback to influence product decisions.
  • Excellent communication skills with the ability to engage at all levels of an organisation.


What's on offer

  • Opportunity to shape strategically important initiatives in a growing international market.
  • Work alongside experienced Product leaders in a collaborative environment.
  • Wellington-based role with flexibility and autonomy.
  • Join a business where product innovation and customer value are core to success.


Applicants must already hold the legal right to work in New Zealand and be Wellington-based. Please note this is not a remote position.

job.title: Head of Health Technology Partnerships
job.description:
• Lead commercial growth across a specialist health technology portfolio.
  • Build partnerships with healthcare providers, technology vendors and sector stakeholders.
  • Growth-focused role within a 100% Māori-owned telecommunications, broadcast and health technology group.


The opportunity
Tū Ātea Network Services is a 100% Māori-owned group operating across telecommunications, broadcasting, media, health technology and infrastructure services.

The organisation is seeking a commercially driven Head of Health Technology Partnerships to grow its health technology portfolio. This is not a clinical, operational or healthcare service delivery role. It is a market-facing commercial role focused on business development, customer growth, strategic partnerships and recurring revenue.

You will work with healthcare providers, aged care organisations, technology partners, suppliers and sector stakeholders to identify new opportunities, grow existing accounts and position Tū Ātea Network Services as a trusted provider of health technology products and services.

Healthcare sector credibility matters, but this role is for someone who can turn relationships into commercial growth.


About you
You may come from health technology, medical technology, digital health, clinical communications, health ICT, enterprise technology, managed services or another healthcare-adjacent commercial environment.

You will bring:

  • Business development, account management or commercial growth experience.
  • Experience selling or partnering across healthcare environments.
  • A track record of revenue growth, account expansion or new market development.
  • Confidence working with healthcare executives, procurement teams, technology partners and senior stakeholders.
  • Strong commercial, negotiation and relationship management capability.
  • The ability to understand customer needs and shape practical technology-led solutions.

This is a strong opportunity for a commercially minded health-sector operator who wants to build a growth portfolio within a Māori-owned technology and infrastructure group.

job.title: Chief Commercial Officer
job.description:
• Lead from the front in winning new business and growing revenue.
  • Build and lead a high-performing, commercially driven sales team.
  • Executive role with genuine influence over market growth and strategy.


The opportunity
We are partnering with an established New Zealand technology and infrastructure services business to appoint a Chief Commercial Officer at an important stage in its growth.

The organisation has significant technical capability, established customer relationships and considerable opportunity to expand its market presence. What it now needs is an exceptional commercial leader who can turn that opportunity into revenue.

Reporting to the Chief Executive, the CCO will take ownership of the commercial growth agenda, with a clear mandate to accelerate new business, grow existing accounts, strengthen market positioning and develop a more proactive, high-performing sales culture.

This is not a role for someone who simply manages relationships, oversees strategy or waits for opportunities to arrive.

We are looking for someone who leads from the front. A commercial leader who is comfortable opening doors, pursuing major opportunities, negotiating complex deals and personally helping to convert business, while building a team capable of doing the same.

You will establish a disciplined approach to business development, pipeline management, account growth and commercial performance. Working closely with product, technical and delivery teams, you will ensure the organisation is taking compelling solutions to market and converting its capability into profitable, recurring revenue.

There is genuine scope to shape the commercial function, establish clear accountability and create the momentum needed for the organisation's next phase.


About you
You will be an accomplished sales and commercial leader with a proven record of delivering significant revenue growth in complex B2B environments.

Your experience may come from technology services, telecommunications, infrastructure, managed services, enterprise solutions or another technically complex, relationship-led sector.

Critically, you will have built business, not simply managed it.

You will bring:

  • Proven new business development: A strong personal track record of identifying opportunities, winning customers, negotiating significant contracts and delivering measurable revenue growth.
  • Sales leadership: Experience building, leading and developing high-performing sales and business development teams, with clear targets, accountability and a strong performance culture.
  • Commercial ownership: Demonstrated accountability for revenue, margin, pipeline performance and sustainable business growth.
  • Strategic customer relationships: The credibility to engage with CEOs, executive teams, major customers and strategic partners, turning relationships into meaningful commercial outcomes.
  • Market development: The ability to identify new markets, develop go-to-market strategies and position complex technical services in ways that resonate with customers.
  • Commercial discipline: Strong deal qualification, forecasting, pricing awareness and negotiation capability, with an understanding of the balance between revenue, profitability and delivery.
  • Entrepreneurial drive: The confidence, pace and initiative to create opportunity and build commercial momentum without relying on a large corporate infrastructure.

You will be equally comfortable in the boardroom and in front of customers. You will know when to set direction, when to empower your team and when to personally get involved to win business.

Above all, you will bring the energy, resilience and commercial ambition to lead a business development function that is proactive, accountable and consistently delivering.


Why consider this opportunity?
This is a genuine opportunity to make your mark on an established business with significant growth potential.

You will have the backing of an ambitious leadership team, strong underlying technical capability and the autonomy to shape how the organisation goes to market.

For someone who enjoys winning business, building teams and creating commercial success, this is an opportunity to have real influence over both strategy and results.

job.title: Chief Information and Security Officer
job.description:
• Enterprise-wide technology infrastructure and security mandate
  • Large-scale, regulated and 24-hour operating environment
  • Direct influence with executive leadership and the Board


SkyCity Entertainment Group is appointing a Chief Information and Security Officer to lead the functions that protect, sustain and strengthen its enterprise technology infrastructure environment.

The mandate spans cyber security, infrastructure and technology operations, site reliability, application support, data engineering and data governance across SkyCity’s gaming, hospitality, entertainment and corporate operations.

Reporting to the Chief Customer and Digital Officer, the CISO will lead the Group’s security and enterprise technology infrastructure. Working alongside the Group Digital Officer, they will ensure SkyCity’s digital ambitions are supported by secure, reliable and efficient platforms and services.

The opportunity is to bring greater integration and effectiveness across a broad enterprise function. This includes strengthening cyber and operational resilience, improving critical service performance, and supporting technology innovation with expedience.

The CISO will provide clear assurance to executive leadership, the Board and the Audit and Risk Committee, and lead the organisation’s response to significant technology and security incidents.

The brief calls for a grounded, assured leader who remains composed under pressure and acts decisively when required. Intellectually curious and externally connected, they will stay ahead of emerging technology infrastructure and security developments, continually looking for better ways to strengthen services, reduce risk and enable the business. They will build trust across technical and business teams, strengthen accountability and bring people with them through change.

We are interested in established CIOs, CISOs and senior technology executives who bring:

  • Leadership experience within a large-scale, complex and continuously operating technology environment.
  • Depth in cyber security, enterprise risk and regulatory assurance.
  • Substantial accountability for infrastructure, technology operations, service delivery and business-critical applications.
  • Experience maintaining resilient 24-hour services and leading the response to major outages or cyber incidents.
  • Strong commercial judgement across investment, vendors and operating models.
  • Credibility with executives, Boards, regulators and senior business leaders.
  • A record of building capable leadership teams and delivering sustained change in complex organisations.

Experience in a regulated, multi-site, customer-facing organisation will be highly regarded.

This is a rare opportunity to influence the technology infrastructure and security direction of one of New Zealand’s most distinctive organisations, and to lead a function central to its resilience, performance and future.

All enquiries and applications will be treated in strict confidence.

job.title: Team Leader, National Standards Committee
job.description:
• Lead a high-performing team delivering meaningful public outcomes
  • Navigate complex and high-profile complaints with confidence
  • Influence the future of legal regulation in New Zealand


The New Zealand Law Society Te Kāhui Ture o Aotearoa plays a vital role in regulating New Zealand's legal profession and maintaining public confidence in legal services. Through the Lawyers Complaints Service, it manages complaints and professional conduct matters that are often complex, sensitive, and of significant public interest.


About the Role
Reporting to the Manager, National Standards & Investigations, you'll lead a highly capable team responsible for supporting National Standards Committees and managing some of the Lawyers Complaints Service's most challenging and high-profile matters.

This is a unique opportunity for a people leader who thrives in complex environments. You'll provide strategic oversight of sensitive complaints, guide and develop an experienced team, identify and manage risk, and ensure matters progress effectively through the regulatory process.

Alongside leading day-to-day operations, you'll have the opportunity to influence process improvements, support organisational change initiatives, and contribute to the ongoing evolution of the complaints service.


What You'll Bring
You're an experienced leader with the confidence to operate in a highly scrutinised environment, balancing strong people leadership with sound judgement and risk awareness.


Ideally, you'll bring:

  • Proven experience leading and developing high-performing teams
  • Experience in complaints, investigations, regulatory, disciplinary, legal, ombudsman, or similar environments
  • Strong stakeholder management and communication skills
  • The ability to navigate complexity, ambiguity, and competing priorities
  • Sound judgement, resilience, and a calm, pragmatic approach under pressure
  • Experience interpreting legislation, policy, or regulatory frameworks is highly desirable.


Why Join?
This is a rare opportunity to lead a highly regarded team working on complex and meaningful matters that help maintain trust in New Zealand's legal profession.

You'll join a collaborative, high-performing team and a supportive leadership environment that values autonomy, fresh thinking, and continuous improvement. Alongside intellectually stimulating work, you'll have the opportunity to influence the future of complaints management and make a lasting impact across the profession.


Apply Now
To submit your application, please click to Apply or for a confidential discussion, contact Fraser Leith at fraser@inside.co.nz. All applications will be acknowledged electronically.

job.title: Commercial Lead
job.description:
• Drive revenue growth, market engagement, and commercial performance
  • Build influential relationships across a professional services environment
  • Shape the future direction of a growing education and events portfolio


About the role:
Reporting into the Commercial Manager, we're seeking a commercially minded and relationship-focused Commercial Lead to drive the growth and performance of a portfolio of professional development programmes, events, and learning solutions.

This is a newly established role created as part of an ambitious growth strategy. You'll identify market opportunities, build trusted industry relationships, and develop a strong pipeline of relevant, high-value offerings that support professionals to stay informed, connected, and ahead of emerging trends.

Working at the intersection of commercial growth, stakeholder engagement, and product development, you'll use market intelligence, industry insight, and customer feedback to identify opportunities, attract leading subject matter experts, and bring new products and services to market.

Success in this role will be measured through revenue growth, increased market engagement, stronger industry partnerships, and the development of commercially successful products that respond to evolving professional needs.


Key responsibilities:

  • Drive revenue growth and portfolio performance through the development of commercially successful products, services, and learning solutions.
  • Build trusted relationships across the profession, engaging industry leaders, stakeholders, presenters, and subject matter experts to create valuable partnerships and opportunities.
  • Stay ahead of market trends, identifying emerging issues, legislative developments, and customer needs to inform product development and commercial decision-making.


What you'll bring:
You are commercially astute, naturally curious, and thrive on building meaningful professional relationships. You enjoy identifying opportunities, influencing stakeholders, and turning ideas into successful commercial outcomes.


You'll also bring:

  • Experience in professional services, legal, consulting, recruitment, membership, education, financial services, or a similar relationship-led environment
  • A proven track record in business development, partnership management, account management, or commercial growth
  • Strong relationship-building and stakeholder engagement skills
  • The confidence and credibility to engage with senior professionals and subject matter experts
  • Strong research, market awareness, and opportunity-spotting capability
  • A proactive, self-directed approach and the ability to work autonomously


What we offer:
This is an exciting opportunity to join a purpose-led organisation at a time of growth and transformation. You'll have the opportunity to shape the role, build an influential professional network, and make a meaningful contribution to the future success of a highly respected organisation.

We offer a collaborative and supportive culture, flexible hybrid working arrangements, and the chance to work alongside people committed to professional excellence and continuous learning.

To submit your application, please click “Apply now”. For a confidential discussion, contact Fraser Leith at fraser@inside.co.nz. All applications will be acknowledged electronically.

job.title: Legal and Commercial Advisor
job.description:
• Direct exposure to high impact investment decisions
  • Blend of legal, commercial and governance work
  • Visible role in a newly established Crown Entity


Join Invest New Zealand at an exciting moment in our journey. We’re a recently established Autonomous Crown Entity with a high-performance, collaborative culture — and we’re looking for a curious, practical legal professional who enjoys working at the intersection of investment, governance, and great process.


About us
Our purpose is to increase the flow of foreign direct investment into sectors with high growth and productivity potential — supporting long-term economic prosperity. We work on investments typically in the $100m to $1b range and help deliver the investment component of the Active Investor Plus (AIP) Visa scheme.


The opportunity
As our Legal & Commercial Advisor, you’ll play a key role in how we assess and support acceptable investments under the AIP visa programme. You’ll lead the investment product assessment work and support the AIP decision makers — making sure they have clear, timely information and that decisions and records are managed in line with relevant legal and regulatory requirements.


What you’ll be doing

  • Be the go-to person for queries about AIP investment criteria and process, working closely with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Pre-assess managed fund and direct investment applications and prepare clear summaries and recommendations for decision makers.
  • Maintain accurate records, including processes/procedures and material correspondence with applicants.
  • Own key risk management processes for the programme, including re-certification and the risk log.
  • Support relationships with key stakeholders such as Government agencies, fund managers and licensed immigration advisers.
  • Assist the General Counsel with Official Information Act requests from time to time.


What you’ll bring

  • An admitted lawyer (commerce and/or finance qualifications are an advantage).
  • 4–6 years’ PQE, including at least 2 years in private practice.
  • Strong commercial judgement and a sound understanding of the managed funds environment (or the motivation to learn quickly, supported by commercial/financial services experience).
  • Confidence working with governance and reporting requirements; board secretariat or legal executive experience is a bonus.
  • Understanding of New Zealand’s financial services regulatory environment.
  • A detail-focused mindset with the ability to assess and appropriately challenge information.
  • Clear, professional communication skills and the ability to build trusted relationships with a wide range of stakeholders.
  • A naturally curious, collaborative style—you enjoy being part of a small team and pitching in where needed.


Why join us?
You’ll be joining a small, ambitious organisation where your work will be visible and valued. We’re building strong foundations and practical ways of working—so you’ll have genuine scope to improve process, influence how we operate, and work alongside experienced colleagues who care about doing great work (and doing it well together).
